en: O Śrī Vāsudeva, who holds in hand the lotus, the Pāñcajanya conch, the Kaumodakī mace, and the discus that wards off fear; O you whose chest bears the Śrīvatsa mark, the destroyer of the root of all diseases, O Lord of Śrī, O Hara, O Hari, remove all my affliction! 1.

O Govinda, lover of the cowherd boys and protector of the herds of cows; O You whose own limbs are so enchanting that they cling to the bodies of the gopīs; O Beloved of the Goddess of the Earth, who are worshiped by Maheśvara and the foremost of gods; O Śrī Bhūpati, Hara, Hare—remove all my affliction! 2.

O Lord with blue locks adorned by peacock feathers, whose body possesses the luster of a dark rain cloud; O Hero, who is affectionate toward Your devotees, O Lotus-eyed One, O Glorious Sovereign, O Hara, O Hari, remove all my disease! 3.

O King of Glory, whose form is bliss, who preceded Janaka and Anaka-pūrva, O ocean of joy, possessing the tenderness of the moon, with a mind equal toward honor and dishonor, O royal swan—O Hara, O Hari, remove all my affliction! 4.

O Lord whose lotus-feet jingle with the sweet tinkling of jeweled anklets, whose eyes are like lotuses, O source of compassion, whose navel is a lotus, O life-restoring medicine, composed of nectar, O virtuous and delightful Lord of Fortune, O Hara, O Hari, remove all my disease! 5.

O Śauri, hero who is a lion to the elephant-demon Kaṃsa, O King who causes the destruction of the mountain of diseases, O Lord whose lotus-feet are as delightful as a lake for swans and other birds; O Śrī-Bhūpati, remove all my illness! 6.

O Śrī Bhūpati, salutations always be to You, who are the armor against the formidable perils of saṃsāra, the giver of all goals, compassionate, eternal, and composed of pure existence and consciousness; O Hara, O Hari, remove all my affliction! 7.

O Lord of Śrī, O Hara, O Hari! May our prostration be offered day and night to the Blessed One, who is dear to his devotees, the destroyer of the sorrow of worldly existence, the bestower of liberation, and the one served by the multitude of sages; [may he] remove all my afflictions. 8.
Thus ends the Vāsudevāṣṭaka composed by the venerable Nārāyaṇa Guru.
